title: Proton shuttling at electrochemical interfaces under alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75400-2

Alkaline water electrolysis is a cost-effective route to hydrogen production, but its mechanism remains unclear at the molecular level. Here, the authors report an in-situ spectroscopic observation of proton shuttling in hydration shells of cations that can improve water dissociation.

title: Widespread controls of precipitation sensitivity on drought recovery of global forests
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75320-1

Forest recovery after drought is critical for ecosystem resilience under climate change. The authors show that intermediate precipitation sensitivity maximizes drought recovery, whereas climate-driven increases reduce recovery in many forests.

title: Dielectric-dependent hybrid functional based on meta-GGA
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75146-x

A density functional is proposed that combines a modern treatment of semilocal interactions with an exact constraint for long-range dielectric screening. The method achieves gold-standard accuracy for energy levels while being fast and user-friendly.

title: The BRCA1-A complex restricts replication fork reversal-dependent DNA repair in ATM deficient cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75271-7

ATM kinase activity is required for cellular survival to replication fork damaging chemotherapies. Here the authors show that deficiency in the BRCA1-A complex promotes chemotherapy resistance of ATM mutated cells by restoring fork reversal to allow homologous recombination repair.

title: North Pacific meltwater weakens the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and preconditions Heinrich Stadial 1
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75199-y

This study shows that Cordilleran ice discharge to the North Pacific may have triggered AMOC weakening during Heinrich Stadials, potentially destabilizing the European and Laurentide Ice Sheets and leading to Heinrich events.

title: Closed-loop readout of anterior insula high-gamma activity steers value-based decisions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75265-5

Using a closed-loop intracranial brain–computer interface, the authors demonstrate that spontaneous neural fluctuations can causally shape value-based decisions, highlighting the role of ongoing brain activity in human choice variability.

title: Glutamatergic signaling underlies brain structural organization for mathematical and reading abilities in children
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75102-9

Across two independent child cohorts, this study shows that glutamatergic signaling, particularly NMDA receptor distribution, shows reproducible spatial correspondence with brain structural organization supporting math and reading abilities.

title: A likelihood-based method for identifying replay from spike sequences
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74822-2

How the brain replays past experiences beyond spatial memories remains unclear. Here the authors introduce a new method based on neural firing order, revealing structured replay in both the hippocampus and visual cortex.
